metadata.methods_description: Participants wore a 64-channel EEG cap and head-mounted eye tracker while simultaneous PPG and GSR were recorded. Two conditions were tested: a 10-minute naturalistic smartphone interaction task and a 5-minute standardized video viewing task. Hardware TTL synchronization pulses (five pulses at ~1-second intervals for session boundaries, additional pulses every 20 seconds) were embedded in EEG and eye-tracking streams for cross-modal temporal alignment. EEG event markers denoted condition onset/offset (S12/S13 for Smartphone Monitor, S22/S23 for Video Monitor).

citation_details.title: Consciousness as OS and Applications: From Neural Primitive (Density × MA) to Higher-Order Emotions, Identity Formation, and Collective Cohesion
citation_details.author: 仁定 五十嵐
citation_details.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
citation_details.abstract: Description This deposit provides the complete computational materials for Supplement S2 of the paper “Consciousness as OS and Applications” (v2.0, April 23, 2026). Contents • Core engine: DensityMA_OS_HigherOrderEmotions_Full_Integration_Final.py • 17 standalone Python simulation scripts (simulation_01_EmoEEG_MC.py 〜 simulation_17_extreme_physiological_states.py) • Generated high-resolution result graphs (PNG, 300 dpi) for each condition • Full Supplement S2 PDF and main paper PDF The simulations test the robustness of the zero-distance self-embrace loop (nostalgia repair, intentional divergence at the Edge of Chaos, identity shake detection, and Relation_MA dynamics) on top of the Density × MA OS layer. Seventeen diverse synthetic conditions are included, inspired by real neuroimaging datasets (ds005540 EmoEEG-MC, ds003751 DENS, ds007537 smartphone, psilocybin ds006072, TMS-EEG, joint musical hyperscanning, NDE-like surge, end-of-life decline, birth/sexual intimacy/acute illness, etc.). All simulations respect the brain’s ~20 W energy constraint through continuous gradient switching among GNWT, FEP, and IIT applications. Results consistently show Relation_MA stably remains in the ideal range 2.0–2.8 across all conditions, providing direct computational evidence for the paper’s central claim: humans cannot discard the self without ceasing to exist.

citation_details.title: A multimodal dataset of EEG, eye-tracking, and physiological signals during naturalistic smartphone interactions
citation_details.author: Prakash Mishra, Tapan Kumar Gandhi, Saurabh R Gandhi
citation_details.abstract: Abstract Smartphones have become pervasive tools for communication, information consumption, and digital interaction, yet the neurophysiological dynamics associated with naturalistic smartphone use remain insufficiently characterized. Here, we present a multimodal physiological dataset collected during ecologically valid smartphone interaction and a subsequent standardized low-engagement baseline condition. Twenty-three participants engaged with their most frequently used smartphone application (primarily gaming or short form video) for ten minutes, followed by a five-minute passive viewing of a standardized nature video. Simultaneous recordings were obtained from electroencephalography (EEG; 64 channels), wearable eye-tracking, photoplethysmography (PPG), and galvanic skin response (GSR) sensors. Questionnaire-based assessments, including the smartphone addiction scale (SAS) and the mobile phone problematic use scale (MPPUS), are also collected to characterize individual differences in smartphone-related behavioral traits. All data streams are synchronized using transistor-transistor logic (TTL) trigger signals to ensure precise temporal alignment across modalities. The dataset is organized according to the Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) specification and is publicly available on OpenNeuro (Accession Number: ds007537 ). This dataset enables the investigation of neural, ocular, and autonomic responses during smartphone interaction and supports multimodal analysis of diverse smartphone behaviors while preserving ecological validity.
